title: Native symmetric derived tensor and one-K-flat localization comparisons
statement: Let C be a category in object universe c and morphism universe v, J a topology, and R a commutative-ring sheaf in max(c,v,u), with the stated additive sheafification hypotheses. In any chosen derived-category universe w, the usual native localization tensor on the unbounded module-sheaf derived category is symmetric monoidal. The canonical lax tensorator of Q is invertible whenever either complex is K-flat in the acyclic-tensor sense. Its inverses give a natural comparison Q(Tot(P tensor L)) ≅ Q(P) tensor Q(L), agreeing with a simultaneous K-flat comparison. The unit comparison is invertible. These comparisons preserve the native complex braiding, associator and both unitors.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 06YT and 0FPT; generic monoidal localization and the usual Koszul signs.

proof.text: Use the existing sheaf localization tensor and its symmetric structure. The independent-universe tensor-Hom adjunction implies colimit preservation in each variable; take countable colimits to totalize unbounded complexes and descend to homotopy classes.
The Koszul braiding on a (p,q) summand is (-1)^(pq) times the sheaf braiding. Applying it twice gives (-1)^(pq+qp)=1. Naturality extends this symmetry through the homotopy quotient.

Functorial flat resolutions give the generic derived monoidal localization. Equality of its braiding and inverse-braiding counits follows from symmetry on homotopy classes, so uniqueness of the derived natural transformations gives involutivity. The existing derived braided construction supplies the two hexagons.

For a complex satisfying the recorded acyclic-tensor condition, symmetry gives the corresponding condition on the other side. The categorical K-flat criterion therefore applies. The derived tensor counit is invertible if either argument is categorically K-flat. Transport this assertion through the natural isomorphism from the complex quotient followed by the homotopy localization to Q.

Invert the lax tensorator on allowed pairs. Its naturality gives naturality of the comparison, and its restriction to pairs of K-flat representatives gives the fixed simultaneous comparison. Invertibility of the unit map follows from that of the quotient and derived localization unit comparisons.

The lax associativity, braidedness and unitality equations can be cancelled against the invertible tensorators and unit map. This yields exactly the representative symmetry, associator and unitor squares. These constructions are valid for the empty site and zero coefficient ring and impose no boundedness or degreewise-flatness hypothesis.

lean.statement:
theorem symmetry_square (P Q : CochainComplex (Modules.{c, v, u} J R) ℤ)
    (hP : CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients (J := J) (R := R) P)
    (hQ : CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients (J := J) (R := R) Q) :
    (tensorIso.{c, v, u, w} J R P Q (Or.inl hP)).hom ≫
        (β_ (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q)).hom =
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (β_ P Q).hom ≫
        (tensorIso.{c, v, u, w} J R Q P (Or.inl hQ)).hom
